PREFACE

   This text is written primarily for those students of sociology, both
advanced undergraduates and graduate students, who actually intend to
engage in social research. Since the vast majority of students in the
social sciences lack a background in college mathematics, this text has
been written so as to avoid mathematical derivationsin so far as possible.
A quick review of certain algebraic principles listed in Appendix 1 should
therefore be sufficient preparation for the average student. But al-
though it is not necessary in a first course in statistics to stress mathe-
matical derivations, the authoris convinced that certain basic and funda-
mental ideas underlying the principles of statistical inference must be
thoroughly understood if one is to obtain more than a mere “‘cookbook”’
knowledge of statistics. For this reason, you will find a relatively heavy
emphasis on the underlyinglogic of statistical inference, including a chap-
ter on probability, with relatively less attention being given to someof the
moreor less routine topics ordinarily discussed in elementary texts.
   One of the most difficult problems encountered in the teaching of
applied statistics is that of motivating students, both in enabling them to
overcometheir fears of mathematics andin learning to apply statistics to
their own field of interest. It is for the latter reason that the author
has not attempted to cover a wide range of applications but has selected
examples of primary interest to sociologists. ‘To some extent, examples
have also been chosen from disciplines which border on sociology: fields
such as social psychology, social work, and political behavior. In most
instances each new topic has been illustrated by a single example, under
the assumption that most students will lose track of the basic line of
thought if too many examples are used to illustrate the same point.
Additional examplesare therefore given in the form of exercises at the end
of each chapter. In general, the author has tried to strike a reasonable
compromise between the desirability of stating basic principles as clearly
and concisely as possible and the necessity of repeating some of the more

that most students using this text will already have been exposed to at

made to discuss such topics as the construction of interview schedules,
reliability and validity, experimental design, coding and tabulating, or
various types of scaling techniques or index construction. Most of
these topics are far too complex to be discussed at all adequately in a
general text on statistics.   Nor is the present text intended as a general
reference work treating all of the statistical techniques currently in use in
the social sciences. Instead, an effort has been made to cover certain of
the most important and basic statistical techniques with sufficient thor-

soc201-quiz-1-23may2023-mids-by-miss-meh:
﻿
Question 1:
To construct a histogram, you first list the ___________ scores along the X-axis.
a) Interval
b) Numerical
c) Ratio

Correct answer: a) Interval

Question 2:
Which of the following graph is used to illustrate the differences in two or more variables?
a) Bar graph
b) Box Plot
c) Pie Chart
d) Clustered Bar Graph

Correct answer: d) Clustered Bar Graph

Question 3:
The objective of statistics in sociology is to _______.
a) None of the given options
b) Making inferences about population
c) Identifying the problem
d) Developing the theory

Correct answer: b) Making inferences about population

Question 4:
A command that carries out statistical analyses and calculates descriptive statistics is known as:
a) Data
b) Analysis
c) DataAnalysis
d) Graphs

Correct answer: c) DataAnalysis

Question 5:
Which of the following is used to illustrate the differences in two or more variables?
a) Box Plot
b) Histogram
c) Scatter Plot
d) Pie Chart

Correct answer: c) Scatter Plot

Question 6:
In research, students formulate a hypothesis and make inferences with the help of__________.
a) Statistics
b) Sample
c) Population
d) Parameter

Correct answer: a) Statistics

Question 7:
The ordinal scale consists of a set of categories or values that are:
a) Organized in an ordered sequence
b) Intervals of exactly the same size
c) Ratios of magnitude
d) Different names

Correct answer: a) Organized in an ordered sequence

Question 8:
To construct a bar graph, you typically use which scale of measurement?
a) Nominal
b) Ordinal
c) Interval
d) Ratio

Correct answer: b) Ordinal

Question 9:
Which of the following is used to represent data in the form of a circle divided into sectors?
a) Box Plot
b) Line Graph
c) Scatter Plot
d) Pie Chart

Correct answer: d) Pie Chart

Question 10:
The objective of statistics in sociology is to make inferences about the _______.
a) Sample
b) Population
c) Research question
d) Hypothesis

Correct answer: b) Population

1. The overall t formula (μ₁−μ₂) calculates the:

 a) Population mean difference

 b) Sample mean difference

 c) Overall result difference

 Correct option: a) Population mean difference

2. In independent sample t-test, parametric test requires a _____________ for each individual in the
sample.

 a) Qualitative score

 b) Numerical score

 c) Symbolic score

 Correct option: b) Numerical score

3. In statistical research, equal variances also referred to as:

 a) Heterogeneity of variance

 b) Distribution of variance

 c) Optimization of variance

 d) Homogeneity of variance

 Correct option: d) Homogeneity of variance

4. While running ANOVA in SPSS, if the value of Levene’s test is lesser than 0.5 then the test will be:

 a) Random

 b) Non-random

 c) Significant

 d) Non-significant

 Correct option: c) Significant

5. The estimated standard error has ______________ relationship with sample variance.

 a) Balance

 b) Proportional

 c) Indirect

 Correct option: b) Proportional

6. In t-statistics test, the larger the ______________, the larger will be the error.

 a) Distribution

 b) Standard deviation

 c) Population size

 d) Sample size

 Correct option: d) Sample size

7. The estimated standard error is inversely related to the:

 a) Number of objectives

 b) Distribution method

 c) Sample size

 d) Number of hypotheses

 Correct option: c) Sample size

8. For correcting the bias in the standard error is to combine the two sample variances into a single value
is called:

 a) Standard mean

 b) Pooled variance

 c) Standard variance

 d) Standard deviation

 Correct option: b) Pooled variance

9. While running one-way ANOVA, the data is entered in the _____________ editor.

 a) Data coding tab of SPSS

 b) Data view tab of Excel

 c) Data view tab of SPSS

 d) Data link tab of SPSS

 Correct option: c) Data view tab of SPSS

10. For ANOVA, the denominator of the F-ratio is called:

  a) Standard variance

  b) Standard variable

  c) Standard error

  d) The error term

  Correct option: d) The error term
